patients.label: 9 year old male with glioblastoma multiforme and bilateral optic neuritis during nivolumab therapy

identity_evidence.quote: The patient was a 9 year old male

attribution_limitations: The abstract states the optic neuritis was induced by nivolumab and the conclusions call it an adverse event of nivolumab therapy, while the discussion says nivolumab is probably responsible.

The case presentation gives intravenous corticosteroids at 1 g/day for 5 days, and the discussion ("In our case") gives IV methylprednisolone 30 mg/kg per day, maximum 1 g daily, for 5 days immediately after the diagnosis; both are 5-day intravenous courses after the diagnosis, but the source does not identify them as the same course.
The source says the combination was given as first and second-line treatments but does not say which drug belongs to which line.
"After a week" before the 20/20 visual acuity has no named anchor; the diagnosis, the start of steroids and the end of the 5-day course are all candidate starting points.

The Figure 1B caption describes T1-weighted contrast enhancement of the bilateral optic nerve, while the text describes bilateral thickening on an urgent MRI; the source does not say these are the same study.

The time phrase "Two days after the second dose" is stated for the hospital admission with the visual decline; the onset of the decline is not dated separately, and the diagnosis is dated four days after the decline.

evidence.quote: (A) Magnetic resonance image (MRI) of the patient’s brain demonstrating a left brain hemisphere and brainstem glioblastoma
